## networks: core concepts

::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
- nodes (aka vertices)
- connections (aka edges)
- weighted/unweithted
- directed/undirected
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](img/simple_network.png){height=500}
:::
:::


## what is Network Analysis?

::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
- study of relationships among entities (nodes) and connections (edges).
- widely used in sociology, biology, economics, politics, history, art…
- example: Florentine marriage network in 1430’s:
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](img/medici.jpg){height=500}
:::
:::


## basic network properties

::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
- _Degree_: number of edges per node.
- _Centrality_: measure of a node’s influence.
- _Betweenness centrality_: measures how frequently a node appears on the shortest path between all other nodes in the graph.
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](img/starwars.png){height=500}
:::
:::

## a caveat: it's a representation!

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(stylo)
data(galbraith)
rownames(galbraith) = gsub("_[0-9]+", "", rownames(galbraith))
round(galbraith[1:20,1:12], 2)
```

## a perfect layout?

```{r}
library(DiagrammeR)

grViz("digraph {
  graph [layout = circo, bgcolor = transparent]

  # Define defaults FIRST so ALL nodes inherit them uniformly
  node [shape = circle, style = filled, fixedsize = true, width = 2.5,
penwidth = 2]

  h1 [label = 'legibility\n(explanatory power)', fillcolor = Beige]
  h2   [label = 'reliability\n(insight to data)', fillcolor = LightBlue]
  h3   [label = 'impact\n(visual attractiveness)', fillcolor = Linen]

  # Connect them fully
  h1 -> h2
  h2 -> h3
  h3 -> h1

  # Clean up edge styling for visual symmetry
  edge [arrowhead = normal, arrowsize = 0.8, penwidth = 1.5]
}")
```
